stories.headline: GST rate and procedure changes take effect from 1 November 2026
points: Retreaded tractor tyres move from 18% to 5% GST; psyllium seeds are exempt, per CBIC notifications.
Reverse charge and 2% GST TDS on contracts above ₹2.5 lakh now cover four more scrap-type goods, not just metal scrap.
Hotel, catering and EV transport credit is limited to same-line services, capped at 2.5% central tax where applicable.
stories.why_it_matters: Rate changes, reverse charge, TDS and Section 14 timing rules are core GST topics that CA and CMA students apply in compliance work.
stories.source_title: Goods and Services Tax | GST changes from 1st November 2026: An item-wise guide with Notifications
check_notes: Point 3 says 'catering' credit is capped at 2.5% central tax; the source applies the cap to hotels, outdoor catering and EV transport only, with restaurants and railway catering uncapped. 'Catering' should read 'outdoor catering'.
Point 2 calls the four goods 'scrap-type'; the source lists used cooking oil, plastic waste, tyre scrap and e-waste. Used cooking oil is not really scrap.

Point 2 runs reverse charge and TDS together; the source says reverse charge applies to purchases from unregistered suppliers and the 2% TDS to purchases from registered suppliers on contracts above ₹2.5 lakh.

stories.headline: GST: 2% TDS on scrap goods and e-invoicing for RCM self-invoices
points: Buyers of five scrap-type goods from registered suppliers must deduct 2% TDS if a contract's value exceeds Rs 2.5 lakh.
Suppliers of those five goods can no longer skip registration just because the recipient pays tax under reverse charge.
Firms with turnover above Rs 5 crore must generate an IRN for self-invoices on unregistered RCM supplies and service imports.
stories.why_it_matters: TDS, registration and e-invoicing rules under GST are core compliance topics that CA and CMA students handle in practice and exams.
stories.source_title: CA, CS, CMA | Analysis of Notifications and Circulars for Week Ending 1st November 2026
check_notes: Point 1 says 'buyers' of the goods must deduct TDS, but the source applies the duty only to registered persons buying from other registered persons. The buyer must also be registered.
Point 3 says 'turnover above Rs 5 crore', but the source specifies aggregate turnover above Rs 5 crore in any preceding financial year from 2017-18 onwards.
Calling used cooking oil one of 'five scrap-type goods' is loose wording, and the headline's 'scrap goods' has the same problem.

stories.headline: Maharashtra sets new GST audit selection rules for FY 2023-24
points: Instructions dated 30 Oct 2026 move audit selection to a risk-assessment basis, after flaws seen in FY 2022-23 audits.
Proposals need non-routine revenue risk above Rs. 2 crore in MMR/PMR or Rs. 1 crore elsewhere in the state.
Proposals must carry a draft FORM GST ADT-01; visits up to 30% of selected cases need only zonal approval.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how State GST audits are chosen and run, which is useful for students heading into GST audit and compliance work.
stories.source_title: Goods and Services Tax | Maharashtra GST Audit Selection Guidelines for FY 2023-24 Prescribe Revenue-Risk Thresholds
